title: Nasruddin and the Orchard

full_text:
Nasruddin climbed over a high wall into an orchard to eat sweet figs. The owner suddenly appeared with an iron pitchfork: "What are you doing up in my fig tree, thief?"

Nasruddin sang: "Tweet, tweet! Trill, trill!"

"What kind of noise is that?" roared the furious gardener.

"I am a nightingale!" replied Nasruddin.

"A nightingale?" shouted the man. "I have never heard such a coarse, discordant song!"

"Well," said Nasruddin calmly, "that is because I am only an amateur nightingale who is still taking singing lessons!" The gardener laughed and handed him a basket of figs.
moral: When caught in error, quick wit softens anger and opens the door to laughter.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Nasruddin and the Orchard"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
